title: Partitioned cursor broker + adaptive read-skipping to cut tail dashboard query latency
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Some dashboard queries (esp. tenant-wide funnels and long-time-range breakouts) show heavy tail latency due to a few hot shard scans and long-running cursor hops. Existing solutions (larger prefetch windows, static overscan) either raise cost or increase median latency for small queries.

Proposal overview: Implement a 'Partitioned Cursor Broker' service that mediates dashboard paginated reads across time/tenant shards and performs adaptive read-skipping using a lightweight sample index + per-tenant read-hint cache. Key pieces:

1) Broker layer: A stateless service that coordinates parallel sub-cursors across physical partitions, issues hedged reads only for slow partitions, and performs asynchronous speculative stitching when gaps are detected. This keeps client-facing cursor semantics but avoids single-partition tail stalls.

2) Sample index and skip hints: Compact sampled summaries (approximate density histograms) per time-window/tenant live in a tiered cache (local LRU + cross-DC redis). The broker uses these to decide whether to skip empty ranges, jump to next candidate anchor, or issue full scan. Summaries are inexpensive to update from the usage analytics pipeline during ingestion.

3) Adaptive hedging policy: Instead of static read duplication, use latency percentiles per partition+route to decide when to send duplicate reads to secondary replicas. Hedging thresholds are dynamic and decay over time as partitions stabilize.

4) Graceful fallback: If the broker cannot confidently skip due to missing sample index data, it falls back to current pagination behavior. This minimizes correctness risk.

Motivation and benefits: Expect 40-60% reduction in 95th/99th tail latency for long-range paginated queries without increasing average token/row cost significantly. Also reduces read amplification from large overscan windows.

Trade-offs and concerns:
- Additional component complexity and operational surface (metrics, deploys).
- Potential for stale skip hints causing missed rows: mitigated by conservative stitching and verification checks during page merges.
- Cross-DC cache consistency: design to tolerate eventual consistency and prefer safety over aggressive skipping.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Spike (1 week): prototype broker to orchestrate parallel sub-cursors and return stitched pages (feature-flagged).
- Sampling pipeline work (2 weeks, parallel): add compact summary write stage in analytics ingestion and expose a read API (low QPS) for broker consumption.
- Hedging policy + hint cache (2 weeks): implement thresholding, local cache with eviction, and metrics.
- Canary rollout (1 week): run behind a feature flag for 10% of traffic; measure latency and correctness.
- Gradual rollout and tune (2 weeks).

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Artifacts and links: technical design doc in Confluence, GitHub spike PR, dashboards to measure P50/P95/P99 and read amplification.
acceptance_criteria: Canary runs with feature flag enabled show >=35% reduction in P99 for top 20 longest-running paginated queries compared to baseline
No customer-visible missing rows or ordering regressions for 99.99% of test cases in end-to-end checks
Read amplification (rows scanned per returned row) does not increase by more than 10% on average for covered queries
Broker CPU/memory footprint fits within a single additional 2x service replica; no major infra changes required
Observability: dashboards emitted for per-partition latencies, hedged-read rate, skip-hint hit rate, and stitch error rate
